docs.title: TaxonomyKit
docs.text:
Hierarchical taxonomy toolkit for Go. Load a category tree from the file you already keep it in, validate it, navigate it, localize it, convert it — structure only, you bring the content.

Most applications that classify things end up rewriting the same tree code: a flat list of categories with parent pointers, a function that walks up to build breadcrumbs, another that lists children for a menu, a lookup by slug, and a second language bolted on later. TaxonomyKit is that code once, with the cases ad-hoc versions get wrong handled: nodes with several parents, locale fallback, deterministic ordering, cycle and orphan detection.

Structure, not content

TaxonomyKit never defines what your categories are. It takes nodes from a CSV, PSV or JSON file — or a Go slice — and gives you a validated tree to query. The model is deliberately close to SKOS, so taxonomies can be exchanged with the rest of the world without a redesign.

docs.title: A first look
docs.text:
tree, err := taxonomykit.Build([]taxonomykit.Node{
    {ID: "all", Labels: taxonomykit.Labels{"en": {Name: "All", Slug: "all"}}},
    {ID: "law", Parents: []string{"all"}, Labels: taxonomykit.Labels{
        "en": {Name: "Law", Slug: "law"},
        "es": {Name: "Derecho", Slug: "derecho"},
    }},
    {ID: "patent", Parents: []string{"law"}, Labels: taxonomykit.Labels{"en": {Name: "Patent", Slug: "patent"}}},
})
if err != nil {
    return err
}
tree.Lineage("patent")          // all › law › patent
tree.Breadcrumb("patent", "es") // Derecho (/derecho, es) › Patent (/patent, en)
tree.BySlug("es", "derecho")    // law

Or from the command line:

taxonomykit validate topics.psv
taxonomykit tree topics.psv --lang es

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:
• Installation and Quick Start
  • Concepts — nodes, primary parents, ordering, documents
  • File Formats — CSV/TSV/PSV rows and the JSON document
  • Navigating a Tree and Localization
  • Validation — every problem code and what to do about it
  • CLI Reference

docs.title: CLI Reference
docs.text:
go install github.com/grokify/taxonomykit/cmd/taxonomykit@latest

Every command reads one taxonomy file. The input format is inferred from the file extension (.csv, .tsv, .psv, .json); --from overrides it, and - reads standard input (with --from).

docs.title: Common flags
docs.text: Flag Meaning --from csv\|tsv\|psv\|json input format when it cannot be inferred --default-lang xx default language for flat files (default: the first row's language)

docs.title: validate <file>
docs.text: Prints every structural problem, one per line as code [id@lang]: message, and exits 1 if there are any. On success prints the node count and the languages found.

docs.title: convert <file> --to csv|tsv|psv|json [-o out]
docs.text: Validates, then writes the taxonomy in another format to stdout or -o. Conversion is lossless and deterministic.

docs.title: tree <file> [--lang xx] [--root id] [--depth n]
docs.text: Prints an indented listing, one node per line as Name (id) /slug, names and slugs resolved in --lang with fallback. --root restricts the output to the subtree below a node (its children at depth 0); --depth limits how deep to print.

docs.title: lineage <file> <id> [--lang xx] [--all]
docs.text: Prints the path from the root to the node as Name (id) > Name (id) > …. With --all, prints every path of a multi-parent node, primary first.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 success 1 invalid taxonomy, unreadable file, unknown node, or bad arguments; the reason is on stderr

docs.title: Node
docs.text:
A node is one entry in the taxonomy:

type Node struct {
    ID      string            // canonical, locale-independent identity
    Parents []string          // empty for a root; Parents[0] is the primary parent
    Labels  Labels            // per-language name, slug and alternative names
    Order   *int              // explicit sibling order (optional)
    Attrs   map[string]string // anything else; never interpreted
}

type Label struct {
    Name string   // display name
    Slug string   // URL segment; empty means "no URL in this language"
    Alt  []string // alternative names
}

One id. Legacy taxonomies tend to accrete several identifiers per node — a short code, a slug, a sanitized id for a search index. TaxonomyKit has one canonical ID (lowercase, ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*$) and treats slugs as labels: they can differ per language and are never the identity.

Slugs are never derived. An empty slug means the node has no URL in that language. If you want slugs generated from names, do it before Build; the kit will not guess.

docs.title: Primary parent and polyhierarchy
docs.text: A node may have several parents. Parents[0] is the primary parent, and it is what single-path operations follow: Parent, Lineage, Depth, Breadcrumb, LCA. Parents and Lineages expose every parent and every root path. This keeps the common case (one breadcrumb) simple while preserving the links a single-parent model would have to throw away.

docs.title: Ordering
docs.text:
Everything the tree returns is ordered, and the order is defined:

  1. nodes with Order set, ascending by Order;
  2. then the rest by the default-language Name (case-insensitive, then case-sensitive);
  3. then by ID.

WithOrderBy(OrderByID) skips step 2. Because ordering is settled once at Build, the same input gives the same menus, sitemaps and walk order on every run and on every machine.

docs.title: Tree
docs.text: Build validates the nodes and returns a *Tree: immutable, indexed, safe for concurrent reads. Nodes returned by the tree belong to the tree — read them, don't modify them. Slices returned by the tree are fresh copies.

docs.title: Document
docs.text:
type Document struct {
    Version     string // "1"
    DefaultLang string
    Nodes       []Node
}

The serializable form: one taxonomy ("scheme" in SKOS terms). flat.Read produces one; ParseDocument reads the JSON form strictly; doc.JSON() writes it deterministically; tree.Document() exports a tree back. The JSON Schema for it is generated from these Go types and embedded in the schema package.

docs.title: Default language
docs.text: Every node must have a Name in the default language — it anchors ordering and is the last step of every label lookup. Set it with WithDefaultLang("en") on Build/Validate, or let a Document carry it.

docs.title: Flat files: CSV, TSV, PSV
docs.text:
The flat package reads and writes delimited text with one row per node and language.

Format Delimiter Notes CSV , RFC 4180 quoting via encoding/csv TSV tab no quoting; a cell may not contain a tab PSV \| cells are trimmed of surrounding whitespace; a cell may not contain a pipe

Blank lines and lines starting with # are skipped in every format.

docs.title: Columns
docs.text:
With a header row, column names are matched case-insensitively:

Column Role Required lang (or language) language tag of this row's label; defaults to the document default no parent (or parentid, parent_id) parent id; empty for a root no id node id yes slug URL segment in this language no name (or display, label) display name in this language yes alt alternative names, ;-separated no order explicit sibling order (integer) no anything else stored in Node.Attrs under the header name no

Without a header row, pass a flat.Columns with zero-based positions (-1 for absent roles).

docs.title: How rows merge
docs.text:
Rows are grouped by id; nodes keep first-appearance order.

  • The first row for an id sets Parents[0] from its parent cell.
  • A later row whose parent cell names a different non-empty id adds that parent. This is how a legacy single-parent file that listed a node twice becomes a multi-parent node instead of silently keeping the last parent.
  • A later row with an empty parent cell, or repeating an existing parent, changes nothing about parents — so language rows can leave the parent blank.
  • Each row sets the Name, Slug and Alt for its lang.
  • order is taken from the first row that has one.
lang | parent     | id       | slug     | name
en   | finance    | mortgage | mortgage | Mortgage     ← primary parent
en   | realestate | mortgage | mortgage | Mortgage     ← adds a second parent
es   |            | mortgage | hipoteca | Hipoteca     ← adds a label only

docs.title: Document default language
docs.text: flat.Options.DefaultLang sets it; otherwise the first data row's language is used (or en if the file has no lang column).

docs.title: Writing
docs.text: flat.Write emits a header and one row per node and language, nodes in document order, languages with the default first then sorted, and the first language row repeated once per parent. Output is deterministic, so a read → write → read round trip reproduces the same document and the same bytes.

docs.title: JSON document
docs.text:
{
  "version": "1",
  "defaultLang": "en",
  "nodes": [
    { "id": "all", "labels": { "en": { "name": "All", "slug": "all" } } },
    { "id": "law", "parents": ["all"],
      "labels": { "en": { "name": "Law", "slug": "law" },
                  "es": { "name": "Derecho", "slug": "derecho" } } },
    { "id": "mortgage", "parents": ["finance", "realestate"], "order": 1,
      "labels": { "en": { "name": "Mortgage", "slug": "mortgage", "alt": ["home loan"] } },
      "attrs": { "legacyCode": "mort" } }
  ]
}
  • taxonomykit.ParseDocument is strict: unknown fields are rejected and the version must be "1".
  • doc.JSON() writes two-space-indented, key-ordered output with a trailing newline, so the file diffs cleanly in version control.
  • The JSON Schema is in the schema package (schema.Document() returns the bytes; schema.ID is its $id). It is generated from the Go types with go generate ./schema and committed, so the types stay the source of truth.

docs.title: Choosing a format
docs.text: Keep the taxonomy in whichever form your team edits most comfortably — PSV is pleasant to read and diff by hand; CSV opens in a spreadsheet — and use JSON as the interchange form between tools. taxonomykit convert moves between them losslessly.

docs.title: Library
docs.text:
go get github.com/grokify/taxonomykit

import (
    "github.com/grokify/taxonomykit"      // tree, validation, localization
    "github.com/grokify/taxonomykit/flat" // CSV / TSV / PSV codec
    "github.com/grokify/taxonomykit/schema" // embedded JSON Schema for the document format
)

The library packages depend only on the Go standard library and build with CGO_ENABLED=0. Go 1.26 or later is required.

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
go install github.com/grokify/taxonomykit/cmd/taxonomykit@latest
taxonomykit --help

The CLI is a thin layer over the library; everything it does is available as a function call.

docs.title: Localization
docs.text: Every node carries a Labels map keyed by language tag, and every lookup that returns text takes a language.

docs.title: Language tags
docs.text: Tags are BCP-47, normalized to lowercase with hyphens: en, es, pt-br. NormalizeLang applies the same normalization to input ("EN_us" → "en-us"), so callers can pass whatever their framework gives them. Validate rejects tags that do not look like BCP-47 (lang.invalid).

docs.title: The fallback chain
docs.text:
A lookup in a language the node does not have does not fail; it falls back:

pt-br-x  →  pt-br  →  pt  →  <default language>

FallbackChain(lang, defaultLang) exposes the chain. The default language is the one every node is guaranteed to have (that is what label.default.missing enforces).

docs.title: Lookups
docs.text:
Call Returns Label(id, lang) the Label, the language it was taken from, and whether the node has any usable label Name(id, lang) the name after fallback, or "" Slug(id, lang) the slug after fallback, or "" if no language on the chain has one Breadcrumb(id, lang) the primary lineage as []Crumb{ID, Name, Slug, Lang} Langs() every language that appears in any label DefaultLang() the default

Name and Slug fall back independently: a node with a Spanish name but no Spanish slug gets the Spanish name and the English slug. That is usually what a site wants — show the translation, keep the URL that exists — and Label tells you when it happened.

docs.title: Breadcrumbs that admit their fallbacks
docs.text:
for _, c := range tree.Breadcrumb("patent", "es") {
    if c.Lang != "es" {
        // render with a "not yet translated" hint, or just render
    }
}

docs.title: Slug lookup
docs.text: BySlug(lang, slug) resolves a URL segment to a node using the effective slug of every node in that language — the slug after fallback. Explicit slugs in the requested language win over fallback slugs, so a Spanish derecho resolves to law while the English law does not resolve in Spanish once a Spanish slug exists. Requests in a language the tree has never seen resolve through the chain to one it has.

docs.title: Slug uniqueness
docs.text: By default slugs must be unique per language across the whole tree (slug.duplicate otherwise), which is what flat /<slug>/ URL schemes need. For path-style URLs (/<parent>/<child>/) use WithSlugScope(SlugScopeSiblings) and slugs only need to be unique among siblings.

docs.title: Navigating a Tree
docs.text: All navigation is on a *Tree from Build. Methods take node ids and return *Node values or slices of them; unknown ids return nil, false or -1 rather than panicking. Returned slices are copies; the nodes they point to belong to the tree.

docs.title: Lookup
docs.text: Call Returns Node(id) the node and whether it exists Has(id) existence Len() number of nodes Roots() nodes without parents, ordered BySlug(lang, slug) the node whose effective slug in lang is slug (see Localization)

docs.title: Up
docs.text: Call Returns Parent(id) the primary parent, or nil for a root Parents(id) every parent, primary first Lineage(id) root → … → node through primary parents Lineages(id) every root path; the primary lineage first Depth(id) number of primary-parent edges above the node; roots are 0 LCA(a, b) the deepest node on both primary lineages

docs.title: Across
docs.text: Call Returns Children(id) direct children, ordered Siblings(id) the other children of the primary parent (other roots for a root), ordered

docs.title: Down
docs.text: Call Returns Descendants(id) every node below, depth-first pre-order; a node reachable by two paths appears once Leaves(id) childless nodes below IsLeaf(id) the node exists and has no children

docs.title: Walking
docs.text:
tree.Walk(func(n *taxonomykit.Node, depth int) bool {
    fmt.Printf("%*s%s\n", depth*2, "", n.ID)
    return n.ID != "archive" // false skips this node's subtree
})

tree.WalkFrom("science", fn) // the subtree below a node; its children are depth 0

for n, depth := range tree.All() { // Go 1.23 range-over-func
    ...
}

Walks are depth-first pre-order from the roots in tree order; a node reachable by several paths is visited once, on first encounter.

docs.title: A rendering example
docs.text:
Breadcrumbs, a sidebar menu and an "also listed in" line for a page about mortgage:

crumbs := tree.Breadcrumb("mortgage", lang)        // primary path
menu   := tree.Children(tree.Parent("mortgage").ID) // the section's items
var also []string
for _, path := range tree.Lineages("mortgage")[1:] { // secondary paths
    also = append(also, tree.Name(path[len(path)-2].ID, lang))
}

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text: This walks through the whole kit on a small topic tree: a file, a validated tree, breadcrumbs in two languages, and the CLI.

docs.title: 1. Write the taxonomy as a file
docs.text:
One row per node and language. The parent column names the parent's id; roots have an empty parent.

topics.psv
lang | parent     | id         | slug       | name
en   |            | all        | all        | All
en   | all        | business   | business   | Business
en   | all        | law        | law        | Law
es   |            | law        | derecho    | Derecho
en   | law        | patent     | patent     | Patent
en   | business   | finance    | finance    | Finance
en   | business   | realestate | realestate | Real Estate
en   | finance    | mortgage   | mortgage   | Mortgage
en   | realestate | mortgage   | mortgage   | Mortgage

Two things to notice:

  • law has a second row in Spanish. It adds a label; it does not change the parent (the parent cell is empty, and would be ignored even if it repeated all).
  • mortgage appears under two parents. It becomes a node with two parents; the first row seen (finance) is the primary parent.

docs.title: 2. Validate it
docs.text:
$ taxonomykit validate topics.psv
ok: 7 nodes, languages en,es

A broken file lists every problem and exits 1:

$ taxonomykit validate broken.csv
parent.missing [b]: parent zzz does not exist
slug.duplicate [a@en]: slug "same" is also used by c
taxonomykit: 2 problem(s)

docs.title: 3. Load it in Go
docs.text:
f, err := os.Open("topics.psv")
if err != nil {
    return err
}
defer f.Close()

doc, err := flat.Read(f, flat.PSV, flat.Options{})
if err != nil {
    return err
}
tree, err := doc.Build() // uses doc.DefaultLang, "en" here (the first row's language)
if err != nil {
    return err // the first taxonomykit.Problem
}

docs.title: 4. Ask it questions
docs.text:
tree.Lineage("mortgage")   // all › business › finance › mortgage      (primary parents)
tree.Lineages("mortgage")  // the path above, plus all › business › realestate › mortgage
tree.Children("all")       // business, law   (ordered by name)
tree.Siblings("patent")    // none — patent is law's only child
tree.IsLeaf("patent")      // true
tree.Leaves("business")    // mortgage

for _, c := range tree.Breadcrumb("patent", "es") {
    fmt.Printf("%s (/%s) [%s]  ", c.Name, c.Slug, c.Lang)
}
// All (/all) [en]  Derecho (/derecho) [es]  Patent (/patent) [en]

n, _ := tree.BySlug("es", "derecho") // n.ID == "law"

Every crumb says which language it was resolved in, so [en] on Patent tells you there is no Spanish label yet.

docs.title: 5. Convert and print
docs.text:
taxonomykit convert topics.psv --to json -o topics.json
taxonomykit tree topics.json --lang es
taxonomykit lineage topics.json mortgage --all

All (all) /all
  Business (business) /business
    Finance (finance) /finance
      Mortgage (mortgage) /mortgage
    Real Estate (realestate) /realestate
  Derecho (law) /derecho
    Patent (patent) /patent

The JSON file is the canonical interchange form; see File Formats.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
Build refuses invalid input and returns the first problem; Validate returns all of them so a tool can show the whole list at once. Both take the same options. Problems are sorted by node id, then code, then language.

if ps := taxonomykit.Validate(nodes, taxonomykit.WithDefaultLang("en")); ps != nil {
    for _, p := range ps {
        fmt.Println(p.Code, p.NodeID, p.Lang, p.Message)
    }
}

Problems and Problem both implement error, and Build's error is a Problem, so errors.As works:

_, err := taxonomykit.Build(nodes)
var p taxonomykit.Problem
if errors.As(err, &p) && p.Code == taxonomykit.ProblemCycle { ... }

docs.title: Problem codes
docs.text: Code Meaning Fix id.invalid id is empty or not ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*$ lowercase the id; move the display form to a label id.duplicate the same id appears twice merge the rows (in a flat file, repeated ids are meant to merge — this only fires for []Node input) parent.missing a parent id does not exist add the parent node or fix the id parent.self a node lists itself as a parent remove it; roots have an empty parent parent.duplicate the same parent listed twice on one node remove the repeat cycle the node is on a parent cycle; reported for every node on the cycle break the cycle root.none there are nodes but none without parents clear the parent of the intended root label.default.missing no non-empty Name in the default language add the label, or change WithDefaultLang slug.duplicate two nodes share a slug in one language within the scope change a slug, or use WithSlugScope(SlugScopeSiblings) for path-style URLs lang.invalid a label key is not a BCP-47 tag use tags like en, es, pt-br

docs.title: What is not validated
docs.text:
• Translations gaps. A node missing a label in a non-default language is fine; lookups fall back. (A --strict-lang report is planned for v0.2.)
  • Multiple parents. Polyhierarchy is a feature, not a problem. If you want to know which nodes have several parents, walk the tree and check len(tree.Parents(id)).
  • Semantics. The kit does not know what a category means; it checks the tree is a tree.

docs.title: From the command line
docs.text:
$ taxonomykit validate topics.csv
parent.missing [b]: parent zzz does not exist
slug.duplicate [a@en]: slug "same" is also used by c
taxonomykit: 2 problem(s)
$ echo $?
1

convert and tree refuse invalid input the same way, so a CI step can be as simple as taxonomykit validate topics.psv.

docs.title: Release Notes v0.1.0
docs.text: Release Date: October 14, 2026

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This is the initial release of TaxonomyKit, a Go toolkit for hierarchical taxonomies — category trees, topic trees, product hierarchies, subject classifications. It owns the structure (nodes, parent relations, ordering, per-language labels and slugs) and the operations applications need on it; the content stays in your own CSV, PSV or JSON file.

The release covers the whole of Phase 1 of the roadmap: the core tree, the flat and JSON codecs with a generated schema, and the CLI. SKOS interchange and document operations (subtree, merge, diff) follow in v0.2.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
go get github.com/grokify/taxonomykit@v0.1.0
go install github.com/grokify/taxonomykit/cmd/taxonomykit@v0.1.0

The library has no dependencies outside the Go standard library and builds with CGO_ENABLED=0 on every platform Go supports. The CLI depends on Cobra.

docs.title: A validated tree with polyhierarchy
docs.text: Build turns a flat []Node into an immutable, indexed Tree, or returns the first problem it finds; Validate returns every problem at once with a stable code (cycle, parent.missing, slug.duplicate, …) so a tool can list them. A node may have several parents; the first is the primary parent, which is what Lineage, Breadcrumb and Depth follow, while Lineages enumerates every root path. Sibling order is defined — explicit Order first, then default-language name, then id — so menus and sitemaps never change between builds.

docs.title: Localization that says what it did
docs.text: Labels are keyed by lowercase BCP-47 tag. A lookup in pt-br falls back to pt, then to the document's default language, and every Crumb records the language it was actually taken from, so a site can decide whether to mark a fallback. BySlug resolves a URL segment per language, with explicit slugs taking precedence over fallback slugs.

docs.title: Files in, files out
docs.text: The flat package reads CSV, TSV and PSV with a header row or a column mapping. One row per node and language; a node listed twice under different parents becomes a multi-parent node instead of silently keeping the last parent, which is how legacy single-parent files migrate without losing links. The JSON Document format round-trips byte for byte and ships with a JSON Schema generated from the Go types.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
taxonomykit validate topics.psv              # every problem, exit 1 if any
taxonomykit convert topics.psv --to json     # csv | tsv | psv | json
taxonomykit tree topics.json --lang es       # indented listing with slugs
taxonomykit lineage topics.psv mortgage --all

docs.title: Known Limitations
docs.text:
• One scheme per document; multiple independent trees (facets) are a v0.2 question.
  • No SKOS import or export yet; the model is designed to map onto SKOS and the JSON-LD codec is the first item of Phase 2.
  • Lineage and Depth consider only primary parents. Use Lineages for every path.
  • Returned *Node values belong to the tree and must not be modified.

docs.title: TaxonomyKit — Implementation Plan (PLAN)
docs.text:
Status: Draft Date: 2026-10-14 Repo: github.com/grokify/taxonomykit

This plan sequences the work defined in the PRD and TRD. Roadmap items and phase membership are tracked in ROADMAP.md.

docs.title: Guiding constraints
docs.text:
• Validation first. The rule table (TRD §4) and its fixtures land before navigation, so every later operation is defined only on valid trees.
  • Determinism from the first commit. The ordering rule is implemented in Build and tested with shuffled input before any accessor exists.
  • Core stays standard-library only. Codecs and the CLI are separate packages; the schema generator is build-tagged out.
  • Each phase leaves main building, tested, lint-clean, with the README example compiling.
  • Verify dependency versions (cobra, invopop/jsonschema) at adoption time.

docs.title: Phase 1 — Core tree, codecs, CLI (v0.1.0)
docs.text:
Goal: A consumer can load a legacy PSV topic file, get a validated tree with polyhierarchy and two languages, and render breadcrumbs, menus, and slug lookups from it; taxonomykit validate|convert|tree work from the command line.

Order of work:

  1. Scaffold: go.mod, MIT LICENSE, README, CI (shared grokify Go CI + Lint workflows, CGO_ENABLED=0), CHANGELOG.json.
  2. node.go, validate.go: types, problem codes, every rule with a fixture in testdata/invalid/; Validate returns all problems, Build the first.
  3. build.go, tree.go: indexing (by id, parent→children, child→parents), ordering rule with Order/name/id and WithOrderBy; Node Roots Parent Parents Children Siblings Lineage Lineages Descendants Leaves IsLeaf Depth LCA; walk.go iterators; property tests.
  4. locale.go: tag normalization, fallback chain, Label, Breadcrumb with per-crumb Lang, BySlug with slug-scope option.
  5. flat/: CSV/TSV/PSV reader with header or Columns, comment/blank handling, polyhierarchy-by-repetition, writer; golden tests. schema/: Document JSON, generated schema, embed, tools.go, schemakit lint in CI.
  6. cmd/taxonomykit: validate, convert, tree, lineage; CLI tests.
  7. Release: CHANGELOG, coverage badge, v0.1.0 after CI; first consumer switches from a local replace to the tag.

Verify: PRD §8 rows; a two-language, multi-parent fixture mirroring the first consumer's shape round-trips PSV → Document → PSV byte-identically and yields the expected lineages, including both paths for the multi-parent node.

docs.title: Phase 2 — Interchange and tree operations (v0.2.0)
docs.text:
Goal: Taxonomies move in and out of SKOS, and common maintenance operations are library calls.

Order of work:

  1. skos/: JSON-LD export with fixed context; import of the same subset; round-trip tests; convert --to skos.
  2. Tree operations returning new documents: Subtree(id), Prune(ids), Merge(a, b) with conflict report, Diff(a, b) listing added/removed/moved/relabeled nodes; CLI diff and subtree.
  3. Multiple schemes per document (facets) if a consumer needs it — decision point, not a commitment.
  4. Docs page per package; v0.2.0.

Depends on: Phase 1.

docs.title: Risks and mitigations
docs.text: Risk Mitigation Polyhierarchy makes "the" lineage ambiguous for consumers Primary parent is explicit and first; Lineage is documented as primary-only, Lineages as exhaustive Locale fallback hides missing translations Crumb.Lang and Label report the language actually used; validate --strict-lang xx lists gaps Legacy files with last-wins duplicates change meaning when read as polyhierarchy validate reports every multi-parent node; the consumer reviews once at migration Scope creep toward a CMS or ontology engine PRD non-goals; new relation types require a consumer and a phase

docs.title: TaxonomyKit — Product Requirements Document (PRD)
docs.text: Status: Draft Date: 2026-10-14 Repo: github.com/grokify/taxonomykit

docs.title: 1. Summary
docs.text:
TaxonomyKit is a Go toolkit for hierarchical taxonomies — category trees, topic trees, product hierarchies, subject classifications. It owns the structure (nodes, parent relations, ordering, per-language labels and slugs) and the operations applications need on it (lineage, children, siblings, leaves, descendants, breadcrumbs, slug lookup, validation, conversion); the content stays with the application.

It follows the -kit convention of this organization: a toolkit for working with a kind of artifact the caller already has, in whatever file they keep it in.

docs.title: 2. Problem
docs.text:
Every classifying application rewrites the same tree code and gets the same things wrong:

  • Single-parent assumption. Real taxonomies have nodes that belong in two places (a "Mortgage" topic under both Real Estate and Personal Finance). Ad-hoc loaders keyed by id silently keep the last parent they saw and lose the other link.
  • Localization bolted on. Display names in a second language are added as a parallel table, slugs are either not localized or collide, and there is no fallback rule when a label is missing.
  • Non-deterministic order. Children come out in map order; menus and sitemaps change between builds.
  • No validation. Cycles, orphans, duplicate ids, and duplicate slugs are discovered in production.
  • Three ids per node. Short codes for humans, slugs for URLs, and sanitized ids for a search index accrete over time with no rule for which is canonical.
  • No interchange. The tree lives in a bespoke CSV; there is no path to or from SKOS, the W3C standard for exactly this.

docs.title: 3. Target users
docs.text:
User Need Content sites (glossaries, docs, catalogs) Breadcrumbs, topic menus, "also listed in", letter/topic index pages, localized URLs Product and data teams A validated, versioned taxonomy file with a schema, convertible between CSV, JSON, and SKOS Library authors A small dependency-free tree they can embed for tagging, faceting, or routing

The first consumer is a private content site with a ~150-node, two-language topic tree that previously handled this in PHP and Ruby.

docs.title: 4. Goals (v0.1)
docs.text:
• G1 — Correct tree semantics. Polyhierarchy (multiple parents) with an explicit primary parent; lineage via primary parents, all lineages on request; cycle, orphan, and duplicate detection at build time.
  • G2 — Localization built in. Per-language name, slug, and alternative labels on every node; a defined fallback chain (exact tag → language subtag → default language); per-language slug uniqueness; slug lookup per language.
  • G3 — Determinism. Every slice the tree returns is in a defined order (explicit order, then name in the default language, then id). Same input ⇒ same output, byte for byte, in every codec.
  • G4 — One canonical id. Nodes are identified by a single stable, locale-independent id; slugs and codes are labels, not identities.
  • G5 — Interchange. A flat tabular codec (CSV/TSV/PSV with a language column), a JSON document format with a Go-generated JSON Schema, and a CLI to validate, convert, and print trees. SKOS JSON-LD import/export in v0.2.
  • G6 — Engine-only, dependency-free. Standard library only in library packages (cobra in cmd/ only); no I/O in the core beyond io.Reader/io.Writer.

docs.title: 5. Non-goals
docs.text:
• Not a CMS or admin UI. No editing workflows, no persistence layer; the taxonomy file is the source of truth and lives in the caller's repo or database.
  • Not an ontology engine. No inference, no arbitrary relation types beyond broader/narrower and related; no OWL.
  • Not a tagging or classification service. Assigning items to nodes, counting items per node, and faceted search belong to the application; the kit only provides the tree those features walk.
  • Not a faceted taxonomy (multiple independent trees in one document) in v0.1. One scheme per document; multiple schemes are a v0.2 question.

docs.title: 6. Core concepts
docs.text:
• Node — the unit of classification: ID (canonical, stable, locale-independent), Parents (zero for a root, one or more otherwise; first is the primary), Labels by language tag (Name, URL Slug, optional Alt names), optional explicit Order, and Attrs (opaque string map the kit never interprets).
  • Tree — the validated, immutable, indexed result of Build. All navigation operates on it.
  • Lineage — the path root → node through primary parents (breadcrumb path). Lineages returns every path for multi-parent nodes.
  • Breadcrumb — a lineage resolved for a language: name and slug per crumb with fallback applied.
  • Document — the serializable form: {version, defaultLang, nodes[]}; the flat codec is a projection of the same data.
  • Scheme — SKOS term for one taxonomy; a document is one scheme.

docs.title: 7. Key user flows
docs.text:
// Load, validate, navigate
doc, err := flat.ReadPSV(r, flat.Columns{Lang: "lang", Parent: "parent", ID: "id", Slug: "slug", Name: "name"})
tree, err := taxonomykit.Build(doc.Nodes, taxonomykit.WithDefaultLang(doc.DefaultLang))

for _, c := range tree.Breadcrumb("mortgage", "en") { /* render */ }
tree.Lineages("mortgage")        // [[all business realestate mortgage] [all business finance personal-finance mortgage]]
tree.Children("technology")      // ordered
tree.Leaves("science")           // every leaf under science
tree.BySlug("es", "derecho")     // law

// Convert and validate from the command line
taxonomykit validate topics.psv
taxonomykit convert topics.psv --to json > topics.json
taxonomykit tree topics.json --lang es

docs.title: 8. Success metrics
docs.text: Dimension Target Correctness Property tests: every node appears in exactly one Lineage; Children/Parent are inverses; Leaves ∪ internal = all; validation rejects every malformed fixture Determinism Golden JSON/CSV output diffed in CI; identical across runs and GOMAXPROCS Portability CGO_ENABLED=0, standard library only in the library Usability README example compiles in CI; a tree of 10k nodes builds in < 50 ms Adoption First consumer live on v0.1; a second internal consumer within six months

docs.title: 9. Open questions
docs.text:
1. Explicit order vs. sorted-by-name default. Proposal: nodes with Order set sort first by Order, the rest by default-language name; confirm.
  2. Slug uniqueness scope. Proposal: unique per language across the whole tree (needed for flat /<slug>/ URLs); a WithSlugScope(Siblings) option can relax it for path-style URLs.
  3. SKOS mapping of Parents[0]. SKOS has no "primary broader"; proposal: export all parents as skos:broader and record the primary in a kit-namespaced property.

docs.title: TaxonomyKit — Technical Requirements Document (TRD)
docs.text: Status: Draft Date: 2026-10-14 Repo: github.com/grokify/taxonomykit

docs.title: 1. Architecture overview
docs.text:
A small core package that builds an immutable, validated, indexed tree from a slice of nodes, surrounded by codecs that only produce or consume that slice.

                    taxonomykit (core)
   ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
   │ Node · Label · Labels · Document                   │
   │ Build(nodes, opts) → *Tree  (validate + index)     │
   │ Tree: Node Roots Parent Parents Children Siblings  │
   │       Lineage Lineages Descendants Leaves IsLeaf   │
   │       Depth LCA Walk Breadcrumb BySlug Label        │
   │ Validate(nodes) → []Problem                        │
   └───────────────┬───────────────────┬───────────────┘
                   │                   │
        ┌──────────▼────────┐  ┌───────▼─────────┐   ┌──────────────┐
        │ flat/  CSV TSV PSV│  │ schema/ JSON     │   │ skos/ (v0.2) │
        │ read · write      │  │ Schema (go:embed)│   │ JSON-LD      │
        └──────────┬────────┘  └───────┬─────────┘   └──────┬───────┘
                   └───────────────────┼────────────────────┘
                              cmd/taxonomykit (validate · convert · tree)

Design rules:

  • Core imports only the standard library. cobra in cmd/ only.
  • Tree is immutable after Build. Accessors return fresh slices (never internal storage); the tree is safe for concurrent reads.
  • Everything is ordered. No map iteration reaches output. The ordering rule (§4) is applied once at build and cached.
  • Validation is total. Build returns the first error; Validate returns every problem with node ids, so a CLI can list them all.
  • Errors are returned, never logged. Programmer misuse (nil tree) panics.

docs.title: 2. Module and dependencies
docs.text:
• Module: github.com/grokify/taxonomykit, Go 1.26+
  • Library dependencies: none
  • CLI: github.com/spf13/cobra
  • Schema generation: github.com/invopop/jsonschema in a //go:build ignore generator (schema/gen/main.go) with a tools.go guard; output linted with schemakit lint --property-case camelCase
  • Verify versions at adoption time per convention.

docs.title: 3. Package layout
docs.text:
taxonomykit/
├── node.go          # Node, Label, Labels, Document
├── build.go         # Build, Options (WithDefaultLang, WithSlugScope, WithOrderBy)
├── tree.go          # Tree navigation
├── locale.go        # tag normalization, fallback chain, Breadcrumb, BySlug
├── validate.go      # Validate, Problem, error types
├── walk.go          # Walk, DFS/BFS iterators (iter.Seq2)
├── flat/            # tabular codec: ReadCSV/TSV/PSV, Write*, Columns mapping, comment lines
├── schema/          # document.schema.json (generated), schema.go (//go:embed), gen/
├── skos/            # v0.2: JSON-LD import/export
├── cmd/taxonomykit/ # CLI
├── testdata/        # synthetic fixtures incl. every malformed case
└── docs/specs/

docs.title: 4. Core types and rules
docs.text:
type Node struct {
    ID      string            `json:"id"`
    Parents []string          `json:"parents,omitempty"` // Parents[0] is the primary parent
    Labels  Labels            `json:"labels"`            // keyed by BCP-47 tag, lowercase ("en", "es", "pt-br")
    Order   *int              `json:"order,omitempty"`   // explicit sibling order; nil = sort by name
    Attrs   map[string]string `json:"attrs,omitempty"`   // opaque
}
type Label struct {
    Name string   `json:"name"`
    Slug string   `json:"slug,omitempty"` // empty means "no URL in this language"; never derived from Name
    Alt  []string `json:"alt,omitempty"`
}
type Labels map[string]Label

type Document struct {
    Version     string `json:"version"`     // "1"
    DefaultLang string `json:"defaultLang"`
    Nodes       []Node `json:"nodes"`
}

Rules enforced by Build/Validate:

Rule Problem code ID non-empty, unique, matches ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*$ id.invalid, id.duplicate Every parent id exists; a node is not its own parent parent.missing, parent.self No cycles through any parent edge cycle At least one root; roots have no parents root.none Every node has a label in the default language with a non-empty Name label.default.missing Per language, Slug unique across the tree (default scope) or among siblings (WithSlugScope(SlugScopeSiblings)) slug.duplicate Language tags normalize to lowercase BCP-47; unknown structure is rejected lang.invalid Duplicate parent ids on one node parent.duplicate

Ordering rule (children, siblings, roots, descendants within a level): nodes with Order set come first ascending by Order; then the rest ascending by default-language Name (case-insensitive, then case-sensitive), then by ID. WithOrderBy(OrderByID) switches the name step to id-only.

Locale fallback for Label(id, lang): exact tag → language subtag (pt-br → pt) → default language. Breadcrumb applies it per crumb and reports in each Crumb which language was used (Lang field), so a site can decide whether to show a fallback indicator.

Lineage with multiple parents: Lineage follows Parents[0] at every step; Lineages enumerates all root paths (deduplicated, ordered by the ordering rule applied to each path's second element). Depth is the length of the primary lineage minus one. LCA operates on primary lineages.

Descendants / Leaves / Walk: DFS pre-order through Children; a node reachable by two paths is visited once (first occurrence). Walk and All/Descend iterators use iter.Seq2[*Node, int] with depth.

docs.title: 5. Flat codec (flat/)
docs.text:
• Input: CSV, TSV, or PSV (|-separated, surrounding whitespace trimmed) with a header row, or a Columns mapping for headerless files. Lines starting with # and blank lines are skipped. Columns: lang, parent (empty = root), id, slug (optional), name, alt (optional, ;-separated), order (optional); unknown columns go to Attrs.
  • One row per (node, language). The first row for a node sets Parents; later rows may repeat or omit the parent; a different parent on a later row adds a parent (polyhierarchy by repetition) — this is how legacy single-parent files that listed a node twice become multi-parent documents rather than silently last-wins. Parents[0] is the first parent seen.
  • Output: Write* emits one row per (node, language) in tree order, deterministic.

docs.title: 6. JSON document and schema (schema/)
docs.text: Document round-trips through encoding/json; schema/document.schema.json is generated from the Go types (Go-first), embedded via //go:embed, and exposed as schema.Document() []byte plus schema.Validate(doc) using the standard library's JSON decoding followed by Validate(nodes) (no third-party schema validator in the library).

docs.title: 7. CLI (cmd/taxonomykit)
docs.text:
taxonomykit validate <file>                 # all problems, exit 1 if any
taxonomykit convert <file> --to csv|tsv|psv|json [--columns …] [-o out]
taxonomykit tree <file> [--lang xx] [--root id] [--depth n]   # indented listing with slugs
taxonomykit lineage <file> <id> [--lang xx] [--all]

Input format is inferred from the extension, overridable with --from.

docs.title: 8. SKOS (skos/, v0.2)
docs.text:
• Export: one skos:ConceptScheme, one skos:Concept per node with skos:prefLabel (language-tagged) per label, skos:altLabel for Alt, skos:broader for every parent, skos:narrower inverse, skos:topConceptOf for roots; the primary parent recorded as tk:primaryBroader in a kit namespace. JSON-LD with a fixed @context.
  • Import: the same JSON-LD subset; other serializations are out of scope (no Turtle/RDF-XML parser).

docs.title: 9. Testing
docs.text:
• Table-driven tests per rule in §4 with a fixture per problem code in testdata/invalid/.
  • Property tests (testing/quick-style, seeded): lineage/children inverse relations, leaves ∪ internal = all, deterministic output across shuffled input order.
  • Golden files for flat and JSON output; CLI tests via os/exec on testdata/.
  • Benchmarks: Build and Breadcrumb at 1k and 10k nodes; target < 50 ms build at 10k.
  • golangci-lint clean; coverage badge; CGO_ENABLED=0 build.

docs.title: 10. Publication hygiene
docs.text: Public from the first push: synthetic fixtures only, generic commit messages, no consumer names or data.
